# Commentary Sources for Adventist Sermon Research

This is the reference list of commentaries and Adventist scholars the `sermon-adventist` and `bible-study-deep` skills draw on. Knowing what these are helps verify where an insight comes from before quoting it.

**Anti-fabrication rule:** Never invent commentary content. If you don't know what a specific commentary says about a passage, say so. Direct the preacher to verify in their physical or digital copy.

---

## Primary Adventist Commentaries

These are the denominational reference works. They should be the first stop for any Adventist exegetical question.

| Name | Year | Description | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Andrews Bible Commentary** | 2020 (full) / 2022 (concise 2-vol) | The newest official Adventist commentary. Single-volume scholarly contributors from across the world Adventist scholarly community. Published by Andrews University Press. Replaces SDABC for many practical purposes — current scholarship, accessible writing. | Print, Logos, Kindle. Andrews University Press. |
| **Seventh-day Adventist Bible Commentary (SDABC)** | 1953-1957 (rev. 1976-1980) | The classic 7-volume verse-by-verse Adventist commentary. Edited by F.D. Nichol. Still the most thorough verse-level Adventist treatment of the whole Bible, even though dated. Volume 4 covers Daniel; Volume 7 covers Revelation. | Print, Logos, EGW Writings app (free PDF). |
| **SDA International Bible Commentary (SDAIBC)** | In progress (2020s) | International Adventist scholarly commentary in production by Adventist scholars from multiple cultural backgrounds. Engages latest grammatical, historical-cultural, literary, theological, and archaeological data. | Print volumes as released. |
| **Andrews Study Bible** | 2010 | Full Bible with study notes from Adventist scholars. Useful as a quick-reference overlay on the biblical text itself. | Print, Logos, Andrews app. |

## Adventist Scholars by Specialty

When commentary content is too thin, look to monographs and articles by Adventist scholars who specialize in the relevant area.

### Daniel and Revelation / Apocalyptic / Eschatology

| Scholar | Notable works | Specialty |
|---|---|---|
| **Jacques Doukhan** | *Secrets of Daniel*; *Secrets of Revelation*; *Daniel: The Vision of the End* | Hebrew/Aramaic; literary structure; Jewish background |
| **Hans LaRondelle** | *How to Understand the End-Time Prophecies of the Bible*; *The Israel of God in Prophecy* | Hermeneutics of prophecy; Israel-church continuity |
| **Ranko Stefanovic** | *Revelation of Jesus Christ* commentary | Greek; Revelation structure; covenant theology |
| **Jon Paulien** | *The Deep Things of God*; *What the Bible Says About the End-Time*; *Armageddon at the Door* | Revelation; allusions to OT in Revelation |
| **William Shea** | *Selected Studies on Prophetic Interpretation* (DARCOM vol. 1); various Daniel articles | Daniel chronology; year-day principle |
| **C. Mervyn Maxwell** | *God Cares*, vols. 1-2 (Daniel and Revelation) | Pastoral exposition of Daniel/Revelation |
| **Gerhard Pfandl** | *Daniel: The Seer of Babylon* | Daniel survey for general readers |

### Sanctuary, Atonement, Investigative Judgment

| Scholar | Notable works |
|---|---|
| **Roy Adams** | *The Nature of Christ*; *Investigative Judgment* articles in Adventist Review |
| **Richard Davidson** | *A Song for the Sanctuary*; sanctuary typology articles |
| **Clifford Goldstein** | *1844 Made Simple*; *Graffiti in the Holy of Holies* |
| **Ángel Rodríguez** | *Issues in the Book of Hebrews* (BRI); various sanctuary articles |
| **Frank B. Holbrook** (ed.) | DARCOM (Daniel and Revelation Committee Series) volumes — definitive Adventist treatment of sanctuary doctrine |

## Adventist Periodicals and Journals

For current scholarly Adventist thinking, beyond commentaries:

- **Ministry Magazine** (ministrymagazine.org) — pastoral and theological articles. Searchable archives back to 1928.
- **Adventist Review** (adventistreview.org) — denominational magazine; pastoral and devotional.
- **Andrews University Seminary Studies (AUSS)** — peer-reviewed Adventist scholarship.
- **Journal of the Adventist Theological Society (JATS)** — Adventist scholarly journal.
- **BRI Newsletter / Reflections** — Biblical Research Institute (BRI) — official denominational position papers and articles.

---

## Non-Adventist Commentaries (Use Carefully — Verify Before Quoting)

These are valuable for exegetical depth, original-language insight, and historical/cultural background. **Use them where they strengthen the exegesis without contradicting Adventist distinctives.** Always verify the actual content before paraphrasing or quoting.

### Background and Cultural Context

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| **IVP Bible Background Commentary: New Testament** (Craig Keener) | Single most useful NT background reference. Cultural and historical detail per passage. |
| **IVP Bible Background Commentary: Old Testament** (Walton, Matthews, Chavalas) | OT cultural and archaeological context. |
| **Zondervan Illustrated Bible Backgrounds Commentary** | Visual-rich background, OT and NT sets. |

### Academic Exegesis

| Name | Publisher | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **NICOT / NICNT** | Eerdmans | Solid evangelical scholarship; reliable on theology and background |
| **Word Biblical Commentary (WBC)** | Zondervan | Most thorough academic series; engage with care on sanctuary/eschatology |
| **Baker Exegetical Commentary on the New Testament (BECNT)** | Baker | Technical with transliterated Greek |
| **Pillar New Testament Commentary** | Eerdmans | Academically rigorous, written for ministers |

### Pastoral / Application

| Name | Notes |
|---|---|
| **NIV Application Commentary (NIVAC)** | Three sections per passage: original meaning / bridging contexts / contemporary significance |
| **Christ-Centered Exposition (CCE)** | Helps connect any text back to Christ |
| **Preaching the Word (Crossway)** | Sermon-level treatment by skilled preachers |

### Cautions on Non-Adventist Commentaries

These commentaries will at times contradict Adventist positions on:
- State of the dead (most assume soul immortality)
- Hellfire (most assume eternal torment)
- Sabbath (most teach Sabbath was abrogated or transferred to Sunday)
- Sanctuary / 1844 / investigative judgment (not held outside Adventism)
- Spirit of Prophecy / Ellen White

When using these sources, **flag the disagreement** rather than smuggle a non-Adventist conclusion into the sermon. Example:

> NICNT on Hebrews 9 reads the heavenly sanctuary as primarily symbolic. The Adventist position (LaRondelle, Davidson) reads it as a real heavenly reality with two phases of priestly ministry.

## Free Digital Tools

Useful for word studies and quick reference, especially when paid commentaries aren't accessible:

| Tool | URL | What it offers |
|---|---|---|
| **Blue Letter Bible** | blueletterbible.org | Free word studies, interlinear, Strong's, Thayer's, BDB lexicons; Matthew Henry, JFB, and other older commentaries |
| **Bible Hub** | biblehub.com | Free interlinear, original languages, parallel translations, brief commentary excerpts |
| **EGW Writings** | egwwritings.org | Full Ellen White corpus searchable; the canonical source for verifying EGW quotes |
| **Adventist Heritage** | adventistarchives.org | Pioneer Adventist primary documents |
| **STEP Bible** | stepbible.org | Free original-language tools from Tyndale House |

---

## How This Skill Uses These Sources

When generating `research-notes.md`:

1. **Always reference Andrews Bible Commentary and SDABC by name** when discussing Adventist commentary insights. Be honest if you don't know the specific content — direct the preacher to verify.
2. **Cite Adventist scholars by name** when their specialty matches the passage (e.g., Doukhan on Daniel, Tonstad on Sabbath, LaRondelle on prophecy).
3. **Use non-Adventist commentary** for exegetical depth and background, but **flag disagreements** with Adventist positions explicitly.
4. **Use free tools (Blue Letter Bible, Bible Hub, STEP Bible)** for word studies — these can be fetched live during skill execution where helpful.
5. **Never fabricate** what a commentary says. If unsure, write: *"[Commentary name] likely treats X here — verify in your copy."*

---

## When in doubt: cite the Bible directly

A sermon grounded in careful exegesis of the biblical text — read in context, in the original where useful, and consistent with the Adventist understanding of the whole — is always stronger than a sermon decorated with commentary quotes. Commentaries are servants of the text, never substitutes for it.
